findings.claim_or_location: D.1 stroke paragraph + Bibliography ref 4: "Aroor S, et al. / systematic review & meta-analysis comparing FAST and BE-FAST in acute stroke patients. 2022. Front Neurol. (PMC8837419)" grounding the [4, meta_analysis] BE-FAST-captures-additional-strokes claim.
findings.issue: First-author misattribution (PF-S2-02). Web-verified against the cited PMC8837419: the article at that exact PMC ID is Chen X, Zhao X, Xu F, et al. "A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Comparing FAST and BEFAST in Acute Stroke Patients," Front Neurol 2022 — first author is Xinjie Chen, NOT "Aroor S." Aroor S is the first author of a different FAST/BE-FAST paper (Aroor 2017, Stroke). The journal, year (2022), PMC ID, and the comparative-diagnostic-value claim are all correct, so the source is real and correctly located — but the displayed first author is wrong on a load-bearing comparative claim, which is the misattributed-cite class the rubric calls out.
findings.recommended_fix: Change ref 4 first author from "Aroor S, et al." to "Chen X, et al." (Chen X, Zhao X, Xu F, et al. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Comparing FAST and BEFAST in Acute Stroke Patients. Front Neurol. 2022; PMC8837419). Confirm whether the Aroor 2017 Stroke paper is also intended as a separate anchor; if so, add it as its own numbered ref rather than mislabeling ref 4.

findings.claim_or_location: D.3 Apple Heart Study paragraph: irregular-tachogram PPV "0.71 (95% CI 0.69–0.74) [5, cohort]."
findings.issue: Confidence-level label inaccuracy. Web-verified against NEJM/Perez 2019 secondary restatements: the irregular-tachogram PPV of 0.71 is reported with a 97.5% CI (0.69–0.74), not a 95% CI. The point estimate and interval bounds (0.69–0.74) are correct; only the stated confidence level is wrong. The companion irregular-pulse PPV 0.84 (95% CI 0.76–0.92) is correctly labeled.
findings.recommended_fix: Change "0.71 (95% CI 0.69–0.74)" to "0.71 (97.5% CI 0.69–0.74)" to match the NEJM-reported confidence level.
